_why: Settings for the lean PR reviewer (the default since the ASK-4743 planted-defect control; KIPI_REVIEW_LEAN=0 turns it off). The reviewer runs with --setting-sources '' so NO user, project or plugin settings load, which drops every context-injecting hook. A reviewer that can run Bash must still sit behind the machine-protecting gates, so exactly these hooks are re-attached and nothing else. The project's permission deny list IS re-attached below as permissions.deny, a copy of .claude/settings.json's (test_review_lean.py pins that it holds every project entry): the reviewer reads an untrusted PR tree and its review is posted, so a .env or key read must stay refused. Measured 2026-11-12 with a real lean run before this copy existed: `sudo -n true` ran. The project Bash ALLOW list is copied too, as permissions.allow, and pr-review-agent.sh no longer allows Bash wholesale (--allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob): a headless run refuses any Bash command outside the list, the same as a normal review under the project's acceptEdits mode. Before this copy a lean reviewer could run wget, nc or ssh, which a normal one cannot (round-4 review of #786, round-2 review of #795). Parity, not containment: python3:* and node:* are on the project list, so a socket is reachable in both modes. The hooks are: destructive-op deny (rm -rf, force push, reset --hard), the archived-engagement deny, and the .claude write guard. KIPI_REVIEW_SCRIPTS is exported by pr-review-agent.sh and points at the trusted control checkout, never at the PR tree under review.
